scope: Named people, schools/universities/Inns of Court, geographic names and administrative territories in twenty OCR biographies; repeated mentions preserved. This is an entity-grounding dataset, not a fully normalized career-event ontology.

methodology.retrieval: Public-web search, Wikipedia sitelinks, and web-retrieved Wikidata pages/search results; not a live Wikidata API dump or vector search. Some responses are cached.
methodology.dates: Birth year only when explicitly printed. Semicolon-delimited clauses preserve chronology, ditto expressions, abbreviated dates and OCR. Four-digit years are extracted tokens, not normalized event dates.
methodology.offsets: Zero-based Python/Unicode code-point offsets into biography.source_text; end exclusive. Overlapping institution and city mentions are intentional.
methodology.qid_policy: qid is an accepted contextual entity link; match_relation and mention-level overrides govern interpretation. geographic_qid is a modern proxy only. candidate_qid and rejected_candidates must not be imported as exact matches. Historical boundaries are not inferred.
methodology.unresolved: No verified QID in this pass; does not mean Wikidata lacks an item.
methodology.scope_exclusions: Ordinary offices, departments, learned societies, military formations, books, ships, decorations and most eponyms within award names are outside scope. Unnamed administrators are not expanded into inferred people. Cuthbert Peek is included explicitly as an award eponym.
methodology.school_relations: An institution mention is not automatically an educated-at assertion: fellowships, employment, legal admission and honorary degrees differ. Parent universities are not added solely from college affiliation.

biographies.source_text: ARCHER, SIR GEOFFREY FRANCIS, K.C.M.G. (1920), C.M.G. (1913).—Asst. collr., East Africa Prot., 1st Dec., 1902; attached secretariat, June, 1902 to Mar., 1903; dist.comsnr., 1st Apr., 1907; spec. serv., Northern Frontier, East Africa, 1909; offr. in-charge, May to Dec., 1911; awarded Cuthbert Peak Grant by the R.G.S., 1918, for surveys in E.
